howItWorks.label: How it works
howItWorks.heading: From master to catalog, in four steps
howItWorks.description: The same frame travels the full pipeline. Each step has its own cost control and its own cache.

analyze.title: We analyze the content
analyze.body: The video is scanned and the frames that add new information are picked out —the scene changes, not every single frame—. The result is a timeline of analyzable moments.

detect.title: We detect the products
detect.body: A vision model locates each object with its box, its category and its relationship to the person on screen. Objects keep their identity across frames, so a garment that reappears is not counted twice.

match.title: We search the catalog
match.body: Each crop is compared against your catalog using visual representations. Candidates come out ranked by similarity, with their size and color variants.

publish.title: We publish only what is reliable
publish.body: Every candidate passes through the agreed threshold and through your rules. What meets the criterion is published, what is doubtful goes to a review queue and the rest is not shown.

integration.label: Integration
integration.description: Pause2Shop sits between your content and your shopping experience. It does not touch the signal, it does not replace the player and it does not block playback.
integration.layerNote: Analysis runs offline; the query responds from cache.

meta.title: Technical architecture
meta.description: The full Pause2Shop pipeline: frame capture, detection, deduplication, matching against catalog and threshold-gated publishing.

architecture.label: Architecture
architecture.heading: How it works inside
architecture.intro: This page is the technical detail the landing page deliberately leaves out. It describes the pipeline as it is implemented today, with the real names of each stage, and it separates at the end what works from what depends on an integration or on an agreement.

capture.title: Frame capture
capture.body: Candidate frames are extracted from the video —uploaded, a YouTube link or a screen capture—. Not all of them are analyzed: the aim is the frame that adds new information, so that cost grows with the content and not with the duration.

details.d1: requestVideoFrameCallback (rVFC) to read frames in sync with the player, instead of sampling blindly on a timer.
details.d2: Scene diff to detect the cut and keep one representative frame per shot.
details.d3: Perceptual hash per frame: if the hash repeats, the frame does not go through the model again.
details.d4: Minimum interval between analyses, configurable, as an upper cap on calls per minute of video.

detect.title: Object detection
detect.body: A vision model returns, per frame, the list of objects with their box, category, dominant color and relationship to the person on screen. The relationship matters because it changes the priority: what someone is wearing weighs more than what is in the background.

details.d1: Normalized bounding boxes in coordinates relative to the frame, so the overlay is independent of resolution.
details.d2: worn / held / background relationship, which orders the search queue.
details.d3: Category filter before spending a call: if the category is not active, the object is not searched.
details.d4: Minimum detection threshold, independent of the publishing threshold.

dedupe.title: Tracking and deduplication
dedupe.body: Objects keep their identity across frames and are merged globally when the analysis finishes. Without this stage, a garment visible in twenty shots would generate twenty searches and twenty catalog entries.

details.d1: Tracking identifiers (trackIds) that survive across consecutive frames.
details.d2: Overlap suppression (NMS) over the boxes of the same frame.
details.d3: Selection of the best crop per object: the largest and sharpest of its whole track.
details.d4: Global merge by visual similarity when closing the job, not only between neighboring frames.

match.title: Matching against catalog
match.body: Each crop is searched first in your own catalog, in a cascade from lower to higher cost. The expensive stage is only reached if the cheap ones do not resolve, and each level has its own cache.

details.d1: Cascade: exact hash → perceptual hash → visual embedding → text search.
details.d2: Nearest neighbors over pgvector for the embeddings stage.
details.d3: Variant resolution: size and color are grouped under the same parent product.
details.d4: Every result records the stage that resolved it (matchStage) and its origin, so it can be audited afterwards.

publish.title: Threshold and publishing
publish.body: The matching result is not published directly. It passes through the agreed threshold and through the client's rules, and from there it goes to one of three places: published, review queue, or discarded.

details.d1: Publishing threshold configurable per catalog and per piece of content.
details.d2: Review band below the threshold: what comes close goes to a person, not to the bin.
details.d3: Brand rules and allowlists and blocklists, applied after the score.
details.d4: Full trace per result: scene, frame, stage, score and decision.

works.body: Frame capture, detection by category, tracking and deduplication, cascading matching against your own catalog, cost control per job and review queue. This is what can be checked in the studio.

pilot.body: Threshold values, real catalog coverage and precision metrics depend on each client's content and catalog. They are measured on an agreed set of scenes, they are not taken for granted.

requiresIntegration.body: Consumption from a player or a companion experience happens via API and needs work on the client side. Live analysis is not available: the pipeline is designed for on-demand content.

common.label: Legal
common.draftNotice: This document describes the technical behavior of the system accurately, but it is pending legal review. It does not include details of the responsible entity or contractual clauses: these will be completed before any commercial use.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.intro: What data Pause2Shop touches, where and for how long. The short version: there are no user accounts, no profile is built, and the content that is analyzed is processed to produce matches, not to train anything.

whatWeProcess.title: What is processed
whatWeProcess.body: The content sent for analysis —an image or a video— and the configured product catalog. The analysis produces frames, crops of the detected objects and the proposed matches, with their score and their provenance.

noAccounts.title: No accounts, no profiles
noAccounts.body: The public application has no sign-up, no login and no advertising tracking cookies. The only preference stored in the browser is the chosen language, so as not to ask for it again. No visitor profile is built.

content.title: Content you send
content.body: The video or the image is used to run the analysis and return the result. It is not shared with third parties beyond the analysis providers needed to produce it, and it is not used to train models of our own.

providers.title: Providers
providers.body: Visual analysis relies on external model providers, to which the frames or crops needed to resolve a query are sent. Those providers' credentials live only on the server and never reach the browser. The specific list of providers for a deployment is agreed with the client.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: Frames and crops have a retention policy configurable per deployment: they exist while they are useful for the analysis job and its review. The product catalog and the published matches persist because they are the result of the service.

security.title: Security
security.body: Traffic encrypted in transit, secrets on the server only, and the operations panel behind authentication with the option to disable it entirely. No compliance certification is claimed: none exists today.

terms.heading: Terms of use
terms.intro: Conditions of use for this public demonstration. Pause2Shop is today a technical pilot: these terms reflect that instead of describing a commercial service that has not yet been contracted.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: These terms cover the use of the public application: the presentation page, the analysis studio, the visible catalog and the guided demo. They do not cover any service agreement, which is governed by its own contract.

pilotNature.title: Pilot nature
pilotNature.body: What is offered here is a demonstration of technical capabilities. Analysis results are indicative, availability is not guaranteed and features may change without notice while the pilot is open.

acceptableUse.title: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.body: The service must not be used to analyze content you do not hold the rights to, to attempt to identify people, or to carry out load or intrusion testing without prior written authorization.

content.title: Content and rights
content.body: Whoever sends content declares that they have the right to do so. The products, brands and trade names that may appear in the results belong to their owners; appearing in the catalog source registry implies no commercial relationship or sponsorship.

availability.title: Availability
availability.body: This is a test environment: there may be interruptions, usage limits and disabled features. If an external provider fails, the system prefers to show no result rather than show a doubtful one.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: These terms may be updated as the product advances. The date of last review appears at the beginning of the document.
